newsitem.title: USA: NORDIC SKIING-NORWEGIAN ELDEN BROTHERS STORM TO COMBINED VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: NORDIC SKIING-NORWEGIAN ELDEN BROTHERS STORM TO COMBINED VICTORY.

text.p: Norway's fast-skiing Elden brothers, Trond Einar and Baard Joergen, roared back from 12th place, nearly two minutes behind, to win a Nordic combined World Cup ski relay Sunday.

The brothers, unquestionably the fastest skiers on the Nordic combined tour but only so-so jumpers, beat teammates Halldor Skard and Bjarte Engen Vik by 33.4 seconds in the six-lap race at the Romick Rodeo Arena.
Austrians Felix Gottwald and Mario Stecher, fourth Saturday in the jumping phase of the two-day competition, were third overall, 50.4 seconds back in 18-degree F (-8 C) sunshine.
"Baard had a fast race. I skied a middle race but it was good enough," said Trond Einar Elden, Nordic combined gold medallist at the 1989 world championships.

The two-man sprint event involves 120-metre ski jumping and a 15-kilometre race in tag-team style with each skier racing over a shortened lap, then tagging his partner to continue until they complete the normal 15-km Nordic combined race distance.
The 15-km race begins with a handicap start, according to jump results, so the first skier across the finish wins.
Finns Jari Mantila and Sampaa Lajunen were first after the jumping, starting 18 seconds ahead of Americans Tim Tetreault and Todd Lodwick.
Mantila started too quickly in his first lap and Lodwick was battling sickness, so both teams dropped. The Finns were fourth, 50.8 seconds out, while USA-1 fell to 10th place.
It was the second straight two-man relay win in Steamboat Springs for the Elden brothers.

Norwegian Coach Vegard Granheim smiled in the finish area as he watched four of his skiers don two gold-plated and two silver-plated cowboy hats on the podium. The brothers split $3,700 for their win.
"The Austrians were a surprise -- they skied so well -- but we felt we could do it. We've become used to this altitude (6,500 feet/2,000 metres)," he said, "and the boys are confident."
